ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graphs of the functions $y=x+b$ and $y=ax+4$ intersect at point $P$. What is the solution set of the inequality $x+b>ax+4$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the intersection point of the graphs of the function $y=x+b$ and $y=ax+4$ has an x-coordinate of $1$, \\
it follows that the solution set for the inequality $x+b>ax+4$ is $\boxed{x>1}$.
